Sales KPIs¶

In [55]:
total_revenue = orders["Final_Amount_INR"].sum()
total_orders = orders["Order_ID"].nunique()
total_quantity = orders["Quantity"].sum()

print("Total Revenue: ₹{:,.0f}".format(total_revenue))

1. Monthly Revenue Trend — Line Chart¶

In [40]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

monthly_sales = orders.groupby("Month_Num")["Final_Amount_INR"].sum()

month_names = [
    "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
    "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"
]

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

plt.plot(
    monthly_sales.index,
    monthly_sales.values,
    marker="o",
    linewidth=2
)

plt.title("Monthly Revenue Trend")
plt.xlabel("Month")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (INR)")
plt.xticks(range(1, 13), month_names)

# Show value on each point
for x, y in zip(monthly_sales.index, monthly_sales.values):
    plt.annotate(
        f"₹{y:,.0f}",
        (x, y),
        textcoords="offset points",
        xytext=(0, 8),
        ha="center"
    )

plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

2. Revenue by Category — Bar Chart¶

In [41]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

category_sales = (
    orders.groupby("Category")["Final_Amount_INR"]
    .sum()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

bars = plt.bar(category_sales.index, category_sales.values)

plt.title("Revenue by Category")
plt.xlabel("Category")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (INR)")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Show revenue value on each bar
for bar, value in zip(bars, category_sales.values):
    plt.text(
        bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
        bar.get_height(),
        f"₹{value:,.0f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom"
    )

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

4. Selling Price vs Product Rating — Scatter Plot Chart¶

In [11]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

high_rating = products[products["Avg_Rating"] >= 4]
low_rating = products[products["Avg_Rating"] < 4]

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

plt.scatter(
    high_rating["Selling_Price_INR"],
    high_rating["Avg_Rating"],
    label="Rating ≥ 4",
    alpha=0.7
)

plt.scatter(
    low_rating["Selling_Price_INR"],
    low_rating["Avg_Rating"],
    label="Rating < 4",
    alpha=0.7
)

plt.title("Selling Price vs Product Rating")
plt.xlabel("Selling Price (INR)")
plt.ylabel("Average Rating")

plt.legend()
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Customer KPIs¶

In [56]:
total_customers = customers["Customer_ID"].nunique()
total_customer_spend = customers["Total_Spend_Lifetime_INR"].sum()
average_customer_spend = customers["Total_Spend_Lifetime_INR"].mean()
average_orders_per_customer = customers["Total_Orders_Lifetime"].mean()
repeat_customers = customers["Total_Orders_Lifetime"].gt(1).sum()
repeat_customer_rate = customers["Total_Orders_Lifetime"].gt(1).mean() * 100

print("Total Customers:", total_customers)
print("Total Customer Spend: ₹{:,.0f}".format(total_customer_spend))
print("Average Customer Spend: ₹{:,.0f}".format(average_customer_spend))
print("Average Orders per Customer: {:.2f}".format(average_orders_per_customer))
print("Repeat Customers:", repeat_customers)
print("Repeat Customer Rate: {:.2f}%".format(repeat_customer_rate))

Product Statistical Analysis¶

In [27]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ==========================================
# PRODUCT ANALYSIS - CHART 3 & CHART 4
# ==========================================

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 6))

# ==========================================
# CHART 3 - Product Rating Distribution
# ==========================================

counts, bins, patches = axes[0].hist(
    products["Avg_Rating"].dropna(),
    bins=10
)

axes[0].set_title(
    "Product Rating Distribution",
    fontsize=14,
    fontweight="bold"
)

axes[0].set_xlabel("Average Rating")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Number of Products")

# Values on bars
for count, patch in zip(counts, patches):
    if count > 0:
        axes[0].text(
            patch.get_x() + patch.get_width() / 2,
            count,
            f"{int(count)}",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom"
        )

axes[0].grid(
    axis="y",
    alpha=0.3
)


# ==========================================
# CHART 4 - Product Price vs Rating
# ==========================================

high_rating = products[products["Avg_Rating"] >= 4]
low_rating = products[products["Avg_Rating"] < 4]

axes[1].scatter(
    high_rating["Selling_Price_INR"],
    high_rating["Avg_Rating"],
    label="Rating ≥ 4",
    alpha=0.7
)

axes[1].scatter(
    low_rating["Selling_Price_INR"],
    low_rating["Avg_Rating"],
    label="Rating < 4",
    alpha=0.7
)

axes[1].set_title(
    "Product Price vs Rating Analysis",
    fontsize=14,
    fontweight="bold"
)

axes[1].set_xlabel("Selling Price (INR)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("Average Rating")

axes[1].legend()
axes[1].grid(alpha=0.3)


# ==========================================
# PAGE TITLE
# ==========================================

fig.suptitle(
    "ShopNova - Product Analysis",
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight="bold"
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
